title: FBISE Annual Exam Simulator 10 (Grand Annual Simulator V (Section A 20 Marks))
subject: english-12

questions.question: In 'Using the Scientific Method', dehydration is defined as:

options.A: The removal of water/moisture to inhibit microbial multiplication
options.B: Adding liquid nitrogen to preserve enzymes
options.C: Boiling liquids under high atmospheric pressure
options.D: Exposing vegetables to sulfur dioxide gas

questions.explanation: Dehydration extracts water from foods, denying bacteria and moulds the moisture necessary to reproduce.

questions.question: What is the ultimate message of the first three essays in Book II?

options.A: To illustrate that human life is fragile, dependent on scientific understanding, and demands dedicated mental discipline to progress
options.B: To show that stars control human destiny through astrological alignments
options.C: To argue that college education is useless in the modern world
options.D: To prove that diseases cannot be prevented by sanitation

questions.explanation: These foundational essays examine cosmic context (Jeans), scientific enlightenment (Barnard & Edwards), and disciplined intellectual ambition (Hawkes).

questions.question: What literary device is used in: 'The waters closed over them, and they slept in their muddy grave'?
questions.explanation: Attributing sleep and a grave to drowned books personifies them and creates a poetic metaphor for their disposal.

questions.question: In 'End of Term', how does David Daiches describe his sensations on Monday mornings during school days?

options.A: Excitement to participate in school sports and debates
options.B: A heavy, dismal oppression at the thought of a whole week of school stretching ahead
options.C: Eagerness to meet his beloved headmaster

questions.explanation: Daiches describes waking up on Monday to the maid's voice as a dismal prison sentence, with five full days of arduous grind lying before him.

questions.question: What is the synonym of 'indolence' in student behavior?
questions.explanation: 'Indolence' is habitual laziness, sluggishness, or avoidance of physical/mental exertion.

questions.question: How much money did Leacock intend to deposit when he nervously entered the bank?
questions.explanation: His salary had been raised to fifty dollars a month, and he felt the bank was the only place for his massive savings of fifty-six dollars.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the word 'inauspicious' in describing Christopher's start?

options.B: Unfavorable, unpromising, or suggesting bad luck ahead

questions.explanation: 'Inauspicious' means boding ill, unpromising, or accompanied by negative omens.

questions.question: Why did Headmaster Mr. Welldon accept Churchill into Harrow despite his blank Latin paper?

options.A: Churchill's father was Lord Randolph Churchill, Chancellor of the Exchequer.
options.B: Mr. Welldon took a broad, discerning view of Churchill's general intellect and character beyond mere classical rote learning.
options.C: Churchill paid a bribe to the proctors.
options.D: The Latin paper was misplaced by examiners.

questions.explanation: Churchill credits Mr. Welldon with extraordinary discernment for judging his underlying ability rather than rejecting him for a blank paper.

questions.question: What is the antonym of 'virulent' in microbiology?
questions.explanation: 'Virulent' means extremely severe, harmful, or deadly; its opposite is benign, harmless, or innocuous.

questions.question: Why could Fleming not immediately produce Penicillin as a clinical drug in 1928?

options.A: He was forbidden by British medical authorities.
options.B: Penicillin was extraordinarily unstable and elusive; as a bacteriologist, he lacked the biochemical team and funding to concentrate and purify it.
options.C: He lost his laboratory in a fire.
options.D: The mould refused to grow again.

questions.explanation: Purifying unstable penicillin required advanced chemical engineering, which was only achieved a decade later by Florey and Chain at Oxford.

questions.question: How did Atatürk encourage agricultural production among Anatolian peasants?

options.A: He abolished the hated 'Ashar' (tithe tax on agricultural yield), introduced modern tractors, model farms, and cooperative credit societies.
options.B: He confiscated all farmland for state palaces.
options.C: He imported all wheat from Canada.
options.D: He ordered farmers to become factory workers.

questions.explanation: Abolishing the exploitative tithe tax liberated Turkish peasants, who Atatürk hailed as 'the true masters of the nation'.

questions.question: What aggressive foreign invasion backed by the Allied powers did Mustafa Kemal crush to reclaim Turkish territory?

options.A: The Greek invasion of western Anatolia (Battle of the Sakarya & Great Offensive)
options.B: The Russian conquest of the Caucasus
options.C: An Italian amphibious landing in Cyprus

questions.explanation: Greek forces advanced toward Ankara, but Kemal defeated them at the 22-day Battle of Sakarya (1921) and drove them out of Izmir in September 1922.

questions.question: What was the date of the Queen's Diamond Jubilee mentioned in the early chapters of the novel?
questions.explanation: Chips and Katherine went to London together to watch the magnificent procession of Queen Victoria's Diamond Jubilee in 1897.

questions.question: In the summer of 1896, where did Chips travel on a walking holiday that changed his life forever?

options.A: The Lake District (staying near Wasdale Head and climbing Great Gable)

questions.explanation: Chips went hiking in the scenic Lake District with a colleague, Rowden, where he encountered Katherine Bridges.

questions.question: What is the primary moral of the conflict between Chips and Ralston in Chapter 11?

options.A: Tradition, human affection, and personal loyalty are deeper and more enduring than cold managerial efficiency.
options.B: Headmasters should never speak to older teachers.
options.C: Latin pronunciation must be changed every ten years.
options.D: All old teachers should be dismissed at sixty.

questions.explanation: The episode vindicates the power of beloved human values over soulless technocratic management.

questions.question: What was Ralston's personality and educational philosophy?

options.A: He treated the school like a modern corporate factory, demanding relentless efficiency, modern science laboratories, and high examination scores.
options.B: He believed in teaching only Latin and Greek poetry.
options.C: He wanted all boys to become agricultural farmers.
options.D: He was lazy and let teachers do as they pleased.

questions.explanation: Ralston was an autocratic modernizer who despised old traditions and sought to turn Brookfield into a high-powered bourgeois prep school.

questions.question: In 1916, during the dark days of World War I, why did Headmaster Chatteris visit Mr. Chips at Mrs. Wickett's cottage?

options.A: To invite him to tea in London
options.B: To beg Chips to come out of retirement and return to Brookfield to teach Latin and help manage the school during a severe wartime staff shortage
options.D: To inform him that Brookfield was being closed down

questions.explanation: Young masters had enlisted to fight in France, replacements were incompetent or elderly, and Chatteris was dying of diabetes and desperate for Chips' help.

questions.question: In Chapter 18, on a cold, foggy afternoon in November 1933, who came to visit Mr. Chips at Mrs. Wickett's?

options.A: Linford, a new boy at Brookfield from Shropshire, sent by mischief-makers as a prank to tea with old Chips

questions.explanation: Young Linford was tricked by older boys into believing Chips had invited him; Chips warmly welcomed the lad, fed him tea and walnut cake, and chatted happily.

questions.question: Identify the sentence that uses the correct preposition of dying:

options.A: The brave soldier died from cholera in the trenches.
options.B: The brave soldier died of cholera in the trenches.
options.C: The brave soldier died with cholera in the trenches.
options.D: The brave soldier died by cholera in the trenches.

questions.explanation: One dies 'of' a specific disease (cancer, cholera, fever), dies 'from' an external cause (wounds, exhaustion), and dies 'for' a noble cause.

questions.question: Identify the sentence with the correct use of 'lest':

options.A: Walk carefully lest you should stumble on the rocks.
options.B: Walk carefully lest you may not stumble on the rocks.
options.C: Walk carefully lest you will stumble on the rocks.
options.D: Walk carefully lest you stumble not on the rocks.

questions.explanation: 'Lest' inherently contains a negative meaning ('for fear that') and takes the modal auxiliary 'should' without 'not'.
